summary: Manual design assessment passed. The node now narrows the remaining standalone screen tail to Inbox, Contacts, and Comms, chooses direct migration onto `StyreneScreen` plus screen-local `WidgetResourceScope` ownership, and explicitly leaves Provision workflow ownership as a separate follow-up.
checks: Research explains why Inbox, Contacts, and Comms still duplicate the old mount/resume refresh contract and why Provision is a distinct workflow-owned follow-up.
Decisions choose direct migration onto `StyreneScreen` instead of another standalone-screen helper and keep UI bootstrap explicit while moving daemon refresh into `_load_data()`.
Acceptance criteria require shared load-cycle ownership, truthful local placeholder behavior, and callable worker scheduling for user-triggered async actions.
Implementation notes identify the three target screens, their regression tests, and the base-class touch point only if concrete migration evidence requires it.
